beats.say: Time to build.
This is the biggest station on the exam. Nine tools and ideas. We go fast, one picture each.
beats.label: Station 2.2 · Building the pipelines
beats.head: Nine ideas, one picture each

check.prompt: A subscriber gets the same message twice. What is the usual cause?
options: The ack came after the deadline
check.why: A message that is not acked in time is delivered again.

beats.say: One: Pub/Sub. Think of a post office for events.
Publishers drop messages on a topic. Every subscription gets its own copy.
beats.label: Topic and subscription
beats.head: Every subscription gets its own copy

beats.say: Delivery is at least once. So duplicates will happen. Plan for them.
beats.label: The guarantee
beats.head: At least once = expect duplicates

beats.say: A subscriber must say thanks, or ack, within the deadline. The default is 10 seconds.
beats.sub: to ack, by default. Too slow? It comes again.

beats.say: Need order? Use ordering keys. Made a mistake? Seek back in time, and replay.
beats.label: Two handy tools
beats.head: Ordering keys. Seek to replay.

beats.say: And to copy messages into BigQuery unchanged, use a BigQuery subscription. No Dataflow needed.
beats.label: No code needed
beats.head: BigQuery subscription

beats.say: Two: Apache Beam, the language of Dataflow.
A PCollection is the data. A PTransform is a step. And the pipeline is the whole graph.
beats.label: Three words

beats.say: ParDo works on one element at a time, like a worker on an assembly line.
beats.label: ParDo
beats.head: One element at a time

beats.say: To add things up, use Combine. It pre-adds on each worker, so it scales better than GroupByKey.
beats.label: Combine
beats.head: Combine beats GroupByKey + sum

beats.say: A side input is a small lookup table that every worker can read.
beats.label: Side input
beats.head: A small lookup for every worker

check.prompt: "Close the basket after 60 minutes with no activity." Which window is that?
check.why: A session window closes after a gap with no activity.

beats.say: Three: windows. A stream never ends, so you cut it into pieces.
Always cut by event time: when it happened. Not when it arrived.
beats.label: The rule
beats.head: Event time, not arrival time

beats.say: Fixed windows are like tiles. Every five minutes, a new one. No overlap.
beats.label: Fixed
beats.head: Tiles: no overlap

beats.say: Sliding windows overlap. The last hour, updated every five minutes.
beats.label: Sliding
beats.head: Overlapping: last hour, every 5 minutes

beats.say: Session windows follow the user. They close after a gap with no activity.
beats.label: Session
beats.head: Closes after a gap of silence

beats.say: The watermark is Dataflow's guess that all data up to a time has arrived. After that, data is late.
beats.label: Watermark
beats.head: "I think everything up to here has arrived"

beats.say: The trap: a fixed window for no activity for an hour. That is a session window.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: "No activity for 60 minutes" means a session window.

check.prompt: You must stop a streaming job for maintenance, and lose no data. What do you do?
check.why: Drain stops reading new input and finishes the data in flight.

beats.say: Four: running Dataflow jobs safely.
To stop a streaming job without losing data, drain it. It finishes what is in flight.
beats.label: Stop safely
beats.head: Drain: finish what is in flight

beats.say: Cancel stops at once, and in-flight data is lost.
beats.label: Stop now
beats.head: Cancel: in-flight data is lost

beats.say: To ship a new version and keep the state, use update.
beats.label: Change in place
beats.head: Update: new code, same state

beats.say: For batch jobs that can wait, FlexRS is cheaper. And flex templates let others launch your job.
beats.label: Also know
beats.head: FlexRS saves money. Flex templates share jobs.

beats.say: Five: Dataproc, for teams that already have Spark.
Best practice: one cluster per job. Create it, run the job, delete it.
beats.label: Ephemeral clusters
beats.head: Create. Run. Delete.

beats.say: That works because the data lives in Cloud Storage, not on the cluster.
beats.label: Why it works
beats.head: Data in Cloud Storage, not on the cluster

beats.say: Add cheap Spot workers for extra compute. But never keep data on them.
beats.label: Save money
beats.head: Spot workers: compute only

beats.say: Or skip the cluster completely, with Dataproc Serverless.
beats.label: No cluster at all
beats.head: Dataproc Serverless

beats.say: Six: getting data into BigQuery.
Batch load jobs are free. Use them when minutes of delay are fine.
beats.label: Batch load
beats.head: Batch loads are free

beats.say: For streaming, use the Storage Write API. It gives exactly-once delivery.
beats.label: Streaming
beats.head: Storage Write API: exactly-once

beats.say: For files, Avro and Parquet load fastest. They carry their own schema.
beats.label: Best formats
beats.head: Avro and Parquet load fastest

beats.say: The trap: zipping CSV files to speed things up. A gzip file cannot be read in parallel.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Gzipped CSV loads slower, not faster.

beats.say: Seven, eight and nine, quickly.
Kafka: keep it if your apps already speak Kafka, on the managed service. Otherwise, Pub/Sub.
beats.label: 7 · Kafka
beats.head: Already on Kafka? Keep it, managed.

beats.say: Duplicates: remove them by key, with ROW_NUMBER or MERGE. And never drop bad rows silently.
beats.label: 8 · Cleaning
beats.head: Dedupe by key. Dead-letter bad rows.

beats.say: And AI: bring the model to the data. Call Gemini from SQL in BigQuery, or use RunInference in Dataflow.
beats.label: 9 · AI enrichment
beats.head: Bring the model to the data

beats.say: Recap. The four you must not forget.
Pub/Sub means at least once. Windows use event time.
beats.label: Station 2.2 · 1 of 2

beats.say: Drain to stop safely. And batch loads into BigQuery are free.
beats.label: Station 2.2 · 2 of 2

beats.say: Nine checkpoints wait below. Take your time.
